member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRVTBaseColorRoughness
member.summary: Disable material type when not required by a project. This minimizes shader permutation count for materials with Runtime Virtual Texture Output nodes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRVTBaseColorSpecular
member.summary: Disable family of material types when not required by a project. This minimizes shader permutation count for materials with Runtime Virtual Texture Output nodes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRVTMask4
member.summary: Disable material type when not required by a project. This minimizes shader permutation count for materials with Runtime Virtual Texture Output nodes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRVTWorldHeight
member.summary: Disable material type when not required by a project. This minimizes shader permutation count for materials with Runtime Virtual Texture Output nodes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRVTDisplacement
member.summary: Disable material type when not required by a project. This minimizes shader permutation count for materials with Runtime Virtual Texture Output nodes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseHighQualityRVTHeightSampling
member.summary: Use higher quality sampling of per pixel heightmaps when rendering to Runtime Virtual Texture.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.WorkingColorSpace
member.summary: Choose from list of provided working color spaces, or custom to provide user-defined space.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RedChromaticityCoordinate
member.summary: Working color space red chromaticity coordinates.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GreenChromaticityCoordinate
member.summary: Working color space green chromaticity coordinates.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.BlueChromaticityCoordinate
member.summary: Working color space blue chromaticity coordinates.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.WhiteChromaticityCoordinate
member.summary: Working color space white chromaticity coordinates.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseLegacyLuminanceFactors
member.summary: Default luminance factors: 0 enables the working color space coefficients (default), 1 enables inaccurate legacy coefficients.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ClearCoatEnableSecondNormal
member.summary: Use a separate normal map for the bottom layer of a clear coat material. This is a higher quality feature that is expensive.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod
member.summary: Dynamic Global Illumination Method

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ReflectionMethod
member.summary: Reflection Method

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ReflectionCaptureResolution
member.summary: The cubemap resolution for all reflection capture probes. Must be power of 2. Note that for very high values the memory and performance impact may be severe.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Reducelightmapmixingonsmoothsurfaces
member.summary: Whether to reduce lightmap mixing with reflection captures for very smooth surfaces. This is useful to make sure reflection captures match SSR / planar reflections in brightness.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseHardwareRayTracingwhenavailable
member.summary: Uses Hardware Ray Tracing for Lumen features, when supported by the video card + RHI + Operating System. Lumen will fall back to Software Ray Tracing otherwise. Note: Hardware ray tracing has significant scene update costs for scenes with more than 100k instances.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RayLightingMode
member.summary: Controls how Lumen Reflection rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing. By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.HighQualityTranslucencyReflections
member.summary: Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SoftwareRayTracingMode
member.summary: Controls which tracing method Lumen uses when using Software Ray Tracing.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ScreenTracingSource
member.summary: Specifies which Scene Color texture Lumen's Screen Traces should read from.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RayTracedTranslucentRefractions
member.summary: Whether to use Lumen refraction tracing from surfaces when using harware ray tracing and hit lighting. This will require shader recompilation to compile of translucent card capture Lumen shaders. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MegaLights
member.summary: Whether to use MegaLights by default, but this can still be overridden by Post Process Volumes, or disabled per-light. MegaLights uses stochastic sampling to render many shadow casting lights efficiently, with a consistent low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing, and does not support Directional Lights. Experimental feature.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RayTracedShadows
member.summary: Controls whether Ray Traced Shadows are used by default. Lights can still override and force Ray Traced shadows on or off. Requires Hardware Ray Tracing to be enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ShadowMapMethod
member.summary: Select the primary shadow mapping method. Automatically uses 'Shadow Maps' when Forward Shading is enabled for the project as Virtual Shadow Maps are not supported.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportHardwareRayTracing
member.summary: Support Hardware Ray Tracing features. Requires 'Support Compute Skin Cache' before project is allowed to set this.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TextureLOD
member.summary: Enable automatic texture mip level selection in ray tracing material shaders. Unchecked: highest resolution mip level is used for all texture (default). Checked: texture LOD is approximated based on total ray length, output resolution and texel density at hit point (ray cone method).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.PathTracing
member.summary: Enables the Path Tracing renderer. This enables additional material permutations. Requires Hardware Ray Tracing to be enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GenerateMeshDistanceFields
member.summary: Whether to build distance fields of static meshes, needed for Software Ray Tracing in Lumen, and distance field AO, which is used to implement Movable SkyLight shadows, and ray traced distance field shadows on directional lights. Enabling will increase the build times, memory usage and disk size of static meshes. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DistanceFieldVoxelDensity
member.summary: Determines how the default scale of a mesh converts into distance field voxel dimensions. Changing this will cause all distance fields to be rebuilt. Large values can consume memory very quickly! Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Nanite
member.summary: Whether to enable Nanite rendering.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AllowStaticLighting
member.summary: Whether to allow any static lighting to be generated and used, like lightmaps and shadowmaps. Games that only use dynamic lighting should set this to 0 to save some static lighting overhead. Disabling allows Material AO and Material BentNormal to work with Lumen Global Illumination. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseNormalMapsForStaticLighting
member.summary: Whether to allow any static lighting to use normal maps for lighting computations.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ForwardShading
member.summary: Whether to use forward shading on desktop platforms, requires Shader Model 5 hardware. Forward shading requires MSAA and has lower default cost, but fewer features supported overall. Materials have to opt-in to more expensive features like high quality reflections. Deferred shading does not support MSAA. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.VertexFoggingForOpaque
member.summary: Causes opaque materials to use per-vertex fogging, which costs slightly less. Only supported with forward shading. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SeparateTranslucency
member.summary: Allow translucency to be rendered to a separate render targeted and composited after depth of field. Prevents translucency from appearing out of focus.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TranslucentSortPolicy
member.summary: The sort mode for translucent primitives, affecting how they are ordered and how they change order as the camera moves. Requires that Separate Translucency (under Postprocessing) is true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TranslucentSortAxis
member.summary: The axis that sorting will occur along when Translucent Sort Policy is set to SortAlongAxis.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.LocalFogVolumeApplyOnTranslucent
member.summary: Allow local fog volumes to be combined and rendered over translucent meshes. Only per vertex evaluation is supported as of today. It requires r.SupportLocalFogVolumes to be true

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.FoveationLevel
member.summary: Set the level of foveation to apply when generating the Variable Rate Shading attachment. This feature is currently experimental. This can yield some fairly significant performance benefits on GPUs that support Tier 2 VRS. Lower settings will result in almost no discernible artifacting on most HMDs; higher settings will show some artifacts towards the edges of the view.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DynamicFoveation
member.summary: Allows foveation level to adjust dynamically based on GPU utilization. Level will range between none at the minimum, and the currently selected foveation level at the maximum.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.CustomDepthStencil
member.summary: Whether the custom depth pass for tagging primitives for postprocessing passes is enabled. Enabling it on demand can save memory but may cause a hitch the first time the feature is used.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.CustomDepthwithTemporalAAJitter
member.summary: Whether the custom depth pass has the TemporalAA jitter enabled. Disabling this can be useful when the result of the CustomDepth Pass is used after TAA (e.g. after Tonemapping)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AlphaOutput
member.summary: Enable r.PostProcessing.PropagateAlpha to enforce alpha in scene color (overriding r.SceneColorFormat if necessary) and propagate it through the renderer's post-processing chain. The legacy "Linear color space only" and "Allow through tonemapper" options now map to True and the engine keeps full alpha precision throughout post-processing. This feature can now be toggled without an engine restart.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DeferredSupportPrimitiveAlphaHoldout
member.summary: Enable primitive alpha holdout support in multiple deferred renderer passes. If primitive holdout masks are not to be used, keep this setting disabled for increased performance. Requires "Alpha Output" to be enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Bloom
member.summary: Whether the default for Bloom is enabled or not (postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AmbientOcclusion
member.summary: Whether the default for AmbientOcclusion is enabled or not (postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultFeatureAmbientOcclusionStaticFraction
member.summary: Whether the default for AmbientOcclusionStaticFraction is enabled or not (only useful for baked lighting and if AO is on, allows to have SSAO affect baked lighting as well, costs performance, postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.bDefaultFeatureAutoExposure
member.summary: Whether the default for AutoExposure is enabled or not (postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultFeatureAutoExposure
member.summary: The default method for AutoExposure(postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AutoExposureBias
member.summary: Default Value for auto exposure bias.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ExtenddefaultluminancerangeinAutoExposuresettings
member.summary: Whether the default values for AutoExposure should support an extended range of scene luminance. Also changes the exposure settings to be expressed in EV100. Having this setting disabled is deprecated and can only be done manually using r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.LocalExposureHighlightContrast
member.summary: Default Value for Local Exposure Highlight Contrast.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.LocalExposureShadowContrast
member.summary: Default Value for Local Exposure Shadow Contrast.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MotionBlur
member.summary: Whether the default for MotionBlur is enabled or not (postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultFeatureLensFlare
member.summary: Whether the default for LensFlare is enabled or not (postprocess volume/camera/game setting can still override and enable or disable it independently)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TemporalUpsampling
member.summary: Whether to do primary screen percentage upscale with Temporal AA pass or not.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultFeatureAntiAliasing
member.summary: Selects the anti-aliasing method to use.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MSAASampleCount
member.summary: Default number of samples for MSAA.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.LightUnits
member.summary: Which units to use for newly placed point, spot and rect lights

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.FrameBufferPixelFormat
member.summary: Pixel format used for back buffer, when not specified

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RenderUnbuiltPreviewShadowsingame
member.summary: Whether to render unbuilt preview shadows in game. When enabled and lighting is not built, expensive preview shadows will be rendered in game. When disabled, lighting in game and editor won't match which can appear to be a bug.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseStencilforLODDitherFading
member.summary: Whether to use stencil for LOD dither fading. This saves GPU time in the base pass for materials with dither fading enabled, but forces a full prepass. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EarlyZPass
member.summary: Whether to use a depth only pass to initialize Z culling for the base pass.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EarlyZPassOnlyMaterialMasking
member.summary: Whether to compute materials' mask opacity only in early Z pass. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableCSMCaching
member.summary: Enable caching CSM to reduce draw calls for casting CSM and probably improve performance.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DBufferDecals
member.summary: Whether to accumulate decal properties to a buffer before the base pass. DBuffer decals correctly affect lightmap and sky lighting, unlike regular deferred decals. DBuffer enabled forces a full prepass. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ClearScene
member.summary: Select how the g-buffer is cleared in game mode (only affects deferred shading).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.VelocityPass
member.summary: When to write velocity buffer. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Outputvelocitiesduetovertexdeformation
member.summary: Enables materials with World Position Offset and/or World Displacement to output velocities during the velocity pass even when the actor has not moved. If the VelocityPass is set to 'Write after base pass' this can incur a performance cost due to additional draw calls. That performance cost is higher if many objects are using World Position Offset. A forest of trees for example.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SelectivelyoutputtotheGBufferrendertargets
member.summary: Enables not exporting to the GBuffer rendertargets that are not relevant. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableParticleCutoutsbydefault
member.summary: When enabled, after changing the material on a Required particle module a Particle Cutout texture will be chosen automatically from the Opacity Mask texture if it exists, if not the Opacity Texture will be used if it exists.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GPUSimulationTextureSizeX
member.summary: The X size of the GPU simulation texture size. SizeX*SizeY determines the maximum number of GPU simulated particles in an emitter. Potentially overridden by CVar settings in BaseDeviceProfile.ini.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GPUSimulationTextureSizeY
member.summary: The Y size of the GPU simulation texture size. SizeX*SizeY determines the maximum number of GPU simulated particles in an emitter. Potentially overridden by CVar settings in BaseDeviceProfile.ini.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportglobalclipplaneforPlanarReflections
member.summary: Whether to support the global clip plane needed for planar reflections. Enabling this increases BasePass triangle cost by ~15% regardless of whether planar reflections are active. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GBufferFormat
member.summary: Selects which GBuffer format should be used. Affects performance primarily via how much GPU memory bandwidth used. This also controls Substrate normal quality and, in this case, a restart is required.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseGPUforcomputingmorphtargets
member.summary: Whether to use original CPU method (loop per morph then by vertex) or use a GPU-based method on Shader Model 5 hardware.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MorphTargetMaxBlendWeight
member.summary: Blend target weights will be checked against this value for validation. Absolue values greather than this number will be clamped to [-MorphTargetMaxBlendWeight, MorphTargetMaxBlendWeight].

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportSkyAtmosphere
member.summary: The sky atmosphere component requires extra samplers/textures to be bound to apply aerial perspective on transparent surfaces (and all surfaces on mobile via per vertex evaluation).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectingHeightFog
member.summary: The sky atmosphere component can light up the height fog but it requires extra samplers/textures to be bound to apply aerial perspective on transparent surfaces (and all surfaces on mobile via per vertex evaluation). It requires r.SupportSkyAtmosphere to be true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportExponentialFogMatchesVolumetricFog
member.summary: When enabled, the height fog scattering/ambient/emissive/phase will match the volumetric fog better.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportLocalFogVolumes
member.summary: Enable local fog volume components rendering support. Disable that setting if local fog volumes are not used in a project for increased performance.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportCloudShadowOnForwardLitTranslucent
member.summary: Enable cloud shadow on translucent surface not relying on the translucenct lighting volume, e.g. using Forward lighting. This is evaluated per vertex to reduce GPU cost and requires extra samplers/textures to be bound to vertex shaders. This is not implemented on mobile as VolumetricClouds are not available on these platforms.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.LightFunctionAtlasFormat
member.summary: Select the format of the light function atlas texture.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.VolumetricFogUsesLightFunctionAtlas
member.summary: Enable support for light function on volumetric fog, when the light function atlas is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DeferredLightingUsesLightFunctionAtlas
member.summary: Enable support for light function on deferred lighting (multi-pass and clustered), when the light function atlas is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SingleLayerWaterUsesLightFunctionAtlas
member.summary: Enable support for light function on Single Layer Water when the light function atlas is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TranslucentUsesLightFunctionAtlas
member.summary: Enable support for light function on Translucent material using Forward Shading mode, when the light function atlas is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportIESProfileOnTranslucent
member.summary: Enable IES profile evaluation on translucent materials when using the Forward Shading mode.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportRectLightOnTranslucent
member.summary: Enable rect light evaluation on translucent materials when using the Forward Shading mode.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GpuCrashDebugging
member.summary: Enables vendor specific and in-engine GPU crash analysis tools.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.InstancedStereo
member.summary: Enable single-pass stereoscopic rendering through view instancing or draw call instancing.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileHDR
member.summary: If true, mobile pipelines include a full post-processing pass with tonemapping. Disable this setting for a performance boost and to enable stereoscopic rendering optimizations. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileMultiView
member.summary: Enable single-pass stereoscopic rendering on mobile platforms.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileUseHWsRGBEncoding
member.summary: If true then mobile single-pass (without post-processing) rendering will use HW accelerated sRGB encoding/decoding. Available only on Oculus for now.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.RoundRobinOcclusionQueries
member.summary: Enable round-robin scheduling of occlusion queries for VR.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MeshStreaming
member.summary: When enabled mesh LODs will stream in based on what is visible on screen.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableHeterogeneousVolumes
member.summary: Enable rendering with the heterogeneous volumes subsystem.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ShadowCasting
member.summary: Enable heterogeneous volumes to cast shadows onto the environment.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.CompositewithTranslucency
member.summary: Enable compositing with heterogeneous volumes when rendering translucency.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.WireframeCullThreshold
member.summary: Screen radius at which wireframe objects are culled. Larger values can improve performance when viewing a scene in wireframe.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportStationarySkylight
member.summary: "Stationary skylight requires permutations of the basepass shaders. Disabling will reduce the number of shader permutations required per material. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor." "For a mobile renderer disabling this option does not reduce shader permutations, but may increse GPU performance. It's recommended to disable it if your project does not requiure Stationary or Movable skylights."

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Supportlowqualitylightmapshaderpermutations
member.summary: "Low quality lightmap requires permutations of the lightmap rendering shaders. Disabling will reduce the number of shader permutations required per material. Note that the mobile renderer requires low quality lightmaps, so disabling this setting is not recommended for mobile titles using static lighting. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor."

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportPointLightWholeSceneShadows
member.summary: PointLight WholeSceneShadows requires many vertex and geometry shader permutations for cubemap rendering. Disabling will reduce the number of shader permutations required per material. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor."

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportVolumetricTranslucentSelfShadowing
member.summary: Enable translucent volumetric self-shadow, requires vertex and pixel shader permutations for all tranlucent materials even if not used by any light.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportCloudShadowOnSingleLayerWater
member.summary: Enable cloud shadow on SingleLayerWater. This is evaluated per vertex to reduce GPU cost and requires extra samplers/textures to be bound to vertex shaders. This is not implemented on mobile as VolumetricClouds are not available on these platforms.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableSubstrate
member.summary: Enable Substrate materials (Beta).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Substrateopaquematerialroughrefraction
member.summary: Enable Substrate opaque material rough refractions effect from top layers over layers below.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Substratetranslucentmaterialroughrefraction
member.summary: Enable Substrate translucent material rough refractions effect over background.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Substrateadvancedvisualizationshaders
member.summary: Enable advanced Substrate material debug visualization shaders. Base pass shaders can output such advanced data.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableRoughDiffuseMaterial
member.summary: Enable Rough Diffuse Material. Please note that when Substrate is enabled, energy conservation is forced to ENABLED.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableEnergyConservationonMaterial
member.summary: Enable Energy Conservation on Material. Please note that when Substrate is enabled, energy conservation is forced to ENABLED.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AutomaticallysetMaterialusageflagsineditordefault
member.summary: Whether new Materials should automatically set usage flags in the Editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.OrderedIndependentTransparencyEnable
member.summary: Enable support for Order-Independent-Transparency on translucent surfaces, which remove most of the sorting artifact among translucent surfaces.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseHairStrandsAutoLODMode
member.summary: Enable hair strands Auto LOD mode by default. Otherwise use Manual LOD mode. Auto LOD mode adapts hair curves based on screen coverage. Manual LOD mode relies on LODs manually setup per groom asset. This global behavior can be overridden per groom asset

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportComputeSkinCache
member.summary: Cannot be disabled while Ray Tracing is enabled as it is then required.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportHardwareVariableRateShading
member.summary: Allows selectively shading certain portions of the image at lower rates, using one pixel shader invocation to shade multiple pixels. Rates are selected per-material, or in screenspace by enabling a shading rate image generator (such as Contrast Adaptive Shading or Stereo Foveation). Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.ReduceGPUSkinVertexFactoryshaderpermutations
member.summary: Cannot be enabled while the skin cache is turned off.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultSkinCacheBehavior
member.summary: Default behavior if all skeletal meshes are included/excluded from the skin cache. If Support Ray Tracing is enabled on a mesh, the skin cache will be used for Ray Tracing updates on that mesh regardless of this setting.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SkinCacheSceneMemoryLimitInMB
member.summary: Maximum amount of memory (in MB) per world/scene allowed for the Compute Skin Cache to generate output vertex data and recompute tangents.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportCombinedStaticandCSMShadowing
member.summary: Allow primitives to receive both static and CSM shadows from a stationary light. Disabling will free a mobile texture sampler and reduce shader permutations. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportmovablelightCSMshaderculling
member.summary: Primitives lit by a movable directional light will render with the CSM shader only when determined to be within CSM range. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileLocalLightSetting
member.summary: Select which Local Light Setting to use for Mobile. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enableclusteredreflectionsonmobileforward
member.summary: Whether to enable clustered reflections on mobile forward (including translucency in deferred). Always supported for opaque geometry on mobile deferred. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileAllowDistanceFieldShadows
member.summary: Generate shaders for static primitives render Lightmass-baked distance field shadow maps from stationary directional lights. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportMovableSpotlightShadows
member.summary: Generate shaders for primitives to receive shadow from movable spotlights. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GPUSkinLimit2BoneInfluences
member.summary: Whether to use 2 bone influences instead of the default of 4 for GPU skinning. This does not change skeletal mesh assets but reduces the number of instructions required by the GPU skin vertex shaders. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportDepthOnlyIndexBuffers
member.summary: Support depth-only index buffers, which provide a minor rendering speedup at the expense of using twice the index buffer memory.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Supportreversedindexbuffers
member.summary: Support reversed index buffers, which provide a minor rendering speedup at the expense of using twice the index buffer memory.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileAmbientOcclusion
member.summary: Mobile Ambient Occlusion. Causion: An extra sampler will be occupied in mobile base pass pixel shader after enable the mobile ambient occlusion. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileDBufferDecals
member.summary: Whether to accumulate decal properties to a buffer before the base pass with mobile rendering. DBuffer enabled forces a full prepass. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseUnlimitedBoneInfluences
member.summary: If enabled, a new mesh imported will use unlimited bone buffer instead of fixed MaxBoneInfluences for rendering.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AlwaysUseDeformerForUnlimitedBoneInfluences
member.summary: Any mesh LODs using Unlimited Bone Influences will always be rendered with a Mesh Deformer. This reduces the number of shader permutations needed for skeletal mesh materials, saving memory at the cost of performance. Has no effect if either Unlimited Bone Influences or Deformer Graph is disabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UnlimitedBoneInfluencesThreshold
member.summary: When Unlimited Bone Influence is enabled, it still uses a fixed bone inflence buffer until the max bone influence of a mesh exceeds this value

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.DefaultBoneInfluenceLimit
member.summary: When BoneInfluenceLimit on a skeletal mesh LOD is set to 0, this setting is used instead. If this setting is 0, no limit will be applied here and the max bone influences will be determined by other project settings. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MaximumbonesperSections
member.summary: Max number of bones that can be skinned on the GPU in a single draw call. The default value is set by the Compat.MAX_GPUSKIN_BONES consolevariable. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.PlanarReflectionMode
member.summary: The PlanarReflection will work differently on different mode on mobile platform, choose the proper mode as expect. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.SupportScreenSpaceReflectionsonmobile

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileSupportsGen4TAA

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.FRootMotionSource
member.summary:
Generalized source of Root Motion to a CharacterMovementComponent.
Has priorities and different accumulation modes (override, additive, set, ignore).
RootMotionSources are accumulated from highest priority to lowest, once all values are "finalized" (meaning no more accumulation to those values), root motion accumulation is finished. Having all of translation and rotation in a transform being overridden during root motion accumulation means that CharacterMovementComponent Phys*() functions no longer need to CalcVelocity() since it'll just get overridden anyway.
Some example source possibilities: Full Animation Root Motion (matching only form of root motion we've supported historically): - Overrides all translation axes or rotation or both - Very High priority so it gets applied first and since it is override no other RootMotionSources have an influence that are lower priority - Scale on translation and/or rotation is set to 1 to match animation 1 for 1 - Provides local space transform (character-orientation relative)
- End result: Same as before - overrides velocity/rotation to values in AnimMontage - But can now scale individual translation axes if desired, or instead of override can use "set" to allow other additive sources of root motion to be applied on top of the animation root motion (modify velocity to home root motion melee attacks, etc.)
Jump pad volumes that work during animation root montage attacks - Constant velocity modification Z up, additive and high priority - Attack/melee animation root motion uses "set" instead of "override" to allow other sources - Animation root motion is applied, then the Z up additive of this source is so you are affected by the jump pad
Attack/melee homing - Additive, lower priority so it gets applied after any animation/significant root motion - World space, sourced by logic modifying velocity to go towards nearby enemies - Could point to a UAbilityTask node from the GameplayAbilities system
Character movement controlled by splines/curves in-editor instead of requiring animation tweaks - Same as animation root motion but source from spline/curve data

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.URuntimeOptionsBase
member.summary:
URuntimeOptionsBase: Base class designed to be subclassed in your game.
Supports checking at runtime whether features are enabled/disabled, and changing configuration parameters via console cheats or startup commands.
Add new config properties to your subclasses which default to the desired normal state This can be adjusted via the development-only tools (command line or cvar) or via an override in the config hierarchy to adjust it as needed (e.g., via a hotfix).
In non-Shipping builds, each property will be exposed both as a console variable and as a command-line argument for easy testing during development.
Debug console syntax (disabled in Shipping configurations): prefix.PropertyName Value Command line syntax (disabled in Shipping configurations): -prefix.PropertyName=Value DefaultRuntimeOptions.ini syntax (note that there is no prefix for these): [/Script/YourModule.YourRuntimeOptionsSubclass] PropertyName=Value
Where the prefix is set by the value of OptionCommandPrefix (defaults to "ro" but can be overridden)
You can also change the name of the ini file that settings are gathered from in your derived UCLASS() declaration

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.USaveGame
member.summary:
This class acts as a base class for a save game object that can be used to save state about the game. When you create your own save game subclass, you would add member variables for the information that you want to save. Then when you want to save a game, create an instance of this object using CreateSaveGameObject, fill in the data, and use SaveGameToSlot, providing a slot name. To load the game you then just use LoadGameFromSlot, and read the data from the resulting object.
See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/SaveGame

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMesh
member.summary:
SkeletalMesh is geometry bound to a hierarchical skeleton of bones which can be animated for the purpose of deforming the mesh. Skeletal Meshes are built up of two parts; a set of polygons composed to make up the surface of the mesh, and a hierarchical skeleton which can be used to animate the polygons. The 3D models, rigging, and animations are created in an external modeling and animation application (3DSMax, Maya, Softimage, etc).
See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Engine/Content/Types/SkeletalMeshes/

member.summary: If true, tangents will be stored at 16 bit vs 8 bit precision

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMesh.PostProcessAnimBPLODThreshold
member.summary: * Max LOD level that post-process AnimBPs are evaluated. * For example if you have the threshold set to 2, it will evaluate until including LOD 2 (based on 0 index). In case the LOD level gets set to 3, it will stop evaluating the post-process AnimBP. * Setting it to -1 will always evaluate it and disable LODing.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMeshComponent.ForceCollisionUpdate
member.summary: Forces the cloth simulation to constantly update its external collisions, at the expense of performance. This will help to prevent missed collisions if the cloth's skeletal mesh component isn't moving, and when instead, wind or other moving objects are causing new collision shapes to come into the cloth's vicinity.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMeshComponent.ClothVelocityScale
member.summary: Scale applied to the component induced velocity of all cloth particles prior to stepping the cloth solver. Use 1.0 for fully induced velocity (default), or use 0.0 for no induced velocity, and any other values in between for a reduced induced velocity. When set to 0.0, it also provides a way to force the clothing to simulate in local space. This value multiplies to individual cloth's velocity scale settings, still allowing for differences in behavior between the various pieces of clothing within the same component.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMeshComponent.ResetAfterTeleport

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMeshComponent.DeferKinematicBoneUpdate

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkeletalMeshComponent.LinkAnimClassLayers(UnrealSharp.TSubclassOf{UnrealSharp.Engine.UAnimInstance})
member.summary: Runs through all layer nodes, attempting to find layer nodes that are implemented by the specified class, then sets up a linked instance of the class for each. Allocates one linked instance to run each of the groups specified in the class, so state is shared. If a layer is not grouped (ie. member.summary: Default value of 1 attempts to preserve volume. Smaller values will loose volume by flattening curved surfaces, and larger values will accentuate curved surfaces.

member.summary: Preserve cuts in the mesh surface by locking vertices in place. Increases the quality of the simplified mesh at edges at the cost of more triangles

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FSkeletalMeshOptimizationSettings.LockVertexColorBoundaries
member.summary: Disallow edge collapse when the vertices do not have a common color

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FSkeletalMeshOptimizationSettings.ImproveTrianglesForCloth
member.summary: Better distribution of triangles on 2d meshes, such as flat cloth, but at the cost of potentially worse UVs in those areas. This generally has little or no effect for mesh regions that aren't laid out on a plane intersecting the origin such as the xy-plane. When this is disabled, the planar regions may simplify to fewer large triangles.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkinnedMeshComponent.UseScreenRenderStateForUpdate
member.summary: If set, use the screen render flag instead of the default render flag when processing offscreen-rendering optimizations (such as VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption) that look to reduce animation work when the mesh is not rendered. Using this option can result in meshes that are occlusion culled ceasing to perform animation work. Note that this can however result in shadows not being animated when meshes are not directly visible.

member.summary: Set up an override skin weight profile for this component on the given layer. The values from the secondary layer (if set to have a profile) are applied first, followed by the values from the primary layer. Since skin weight profiles are stored as sparse data, where only weight values different from the base are kept in storage, it's possible to set up layers such that they don't interfere with one another.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.ASkyAtmosphere
member.summary: A placeable actor that represents a planet atmosphere material and simulates sky and light scattering within it. See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/en-US/Engine/Actors/FogEffects/SkyAtmosphere/index.html

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent
member.summary: A component that represents a planet atmosphere material and simulates sky and light scattering within it. See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/en-US/Engine/Actors/FogEffects/SkyAtmosphere/index.html

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.TransformMode
member.summary: The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.TraceSampleCountScale
member.summary: Scale the atmosphere tracing sample count. Quality level scalability The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 0. The sample count is still clamped according to scalability setting to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT.SampleCountMax' when 'r.SkyAtmosphere.FastSkyLUT' is 1. The sample count is still clamped for aerial perspective according to 'r.SkyAtmosphere.AerialPerspectiveLUT.SampleCountMaxPerSlice'.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.TentDistribution
member.summary: Represents the altitude based tent distribution of absorption particles in the atmosphere.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.TransmittanceMinLightElevationAngle
member.summary: The minimum elevation angle in degree that should be used to evaluate the sun transmittance to the ground. Useful to maintain a visible sun light and shadow on meshes even when the sun has started going below the horizon. This does not affect the aerial perspective.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.AerialPerspectiveStartDepth
member.summary: The distance (kilometers) at which we start evaluating the aerial perspective. Having the aerial perspective starts away from the camera can help with performance: pixels not affected by the aerial perspective will have their computation skipped using early depth test.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.StaticLightingBuiltGUID
member.summary: GUID used to associate a atmospheric component with precomputed lighting/shadowing information across levels. The GUID changes whenever the atmospheric properties change, e.g. LUTs.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.GroundRadius
member.summary: The radius in kilometers from the center of the planet to the ground level.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.GroundAlbedo
member.summary: The ground albedo that will tint the atmosphere when the sun light will bounce on it. Only taken into account when MultiScattering>0.0.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.AtmosphereHeight
member.summary: The height of the atmosphere layer above the ground in kilometers.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MultiScattering
member.summary: Factor applied to multiple scattering only (after the sun light has bounced around in the atmosphere at least once). Multiple scattering is evaluated using a dual scattering approach. A value of 2 is recommended to better represent default atmosphere when r.SkyAtmosphere.MultiScatteringLUT.HighQuality=0.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.RayleighScatteringScale
member.summary: Rayleigh scattering coefficient scale.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.RayleighScattering
member.summary: The Rayleigh scattering coefficients resulting from molecules in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.RayleighExponentialDistribution
member.summary: The altitude in kilometer at which Rayleigh scattering effect is reduced to 40%.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieScatteringScale
member.summary: Mie scattering coefficient scale.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieScattering
member.summary: The Mie scattering coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be scattered more.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieAbsorptionScale
member.summary: Mie absorption coefficient scale.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieAbsorption
member.summary: The Mie absorption coefficients resulting from particles in the air at an altitude of 0 kilometer. As it becomes higher, light will be absorbed more.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieAnisotropy
member.summary: A value of 0 mean light is uniformly scattered. A value closer to 1 means lights will scatter more forward, resulting in halos around light sources.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.MieExponentialDistribution
member.summary: The altitude in kilometer at which Mie effects are reduced to 40%.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.AbsorptionScale
member.summary: Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. This approximates ozone molecules distribution in the Earth atmosphere.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.Absorption
member.summary: Absorption coefficients for another atmosphere layer. Density increase from 0 to 1 between 10 to 25km and decreases from 1 to 0 between 25 to 40km. The default values represents ozone molecules absorption in the Earth atmosphere.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.SkyLuminanceFactor
member.summary: Scales the luminance of pixels representing the sky. This will impact the captured sky light.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.AerialPerspectiveViewDistanceScale
member.summary: Makes the aerial perspective look thicker by scaling distances from view to surfaces (opaque and translucent).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.HeightFogContribution
member.summary: Scale the sky and atmosphere lights contribution to the height fog when SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog project setting is true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.Holdout
member.summary: If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.RenderInMainPass
member.summary: If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyAtmosphereComponent.GetAtmosphericLightToMatchIlluminanceOnGround(UnrealSharp.CoreUObject.FVector,System.Single)
member.summary: This function can be used for instance in order to evaluate a directional atmospheric light outer space illuminance for a desired illuminance on ground given a direction. This is given for the position at the top of the virtual planet. Plus the output outer space illuminance into the light intensity.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.CloudAmbientOcclusion
member.summary: Whether the cloud should occlude sky contribution within the atmosphere (progressively fading multiple scattering out) or not.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.CloudAmbientOcclusionStrength
member.summary: The strength of the ambient occlusion, higher value will block more light.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.CloudAmbientOcclusionExtent
member.summary: The world space radius of the cloud ambient occlusion map around the camera in kilometers.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.CloudAmbientOcclusionMapResolutionScale
member.summary: Scale the cloud ambient occlusion map resolution, base resolution is 512. The resolution is still clamped to 'r.VolumetricCloud.SkyAO.MaxResolution'.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.CloudAmbientOcclusionApertureScale
member.summary: Controls the cone aperture angle over which the sky occlusion due to volumetric clouds is evaluated. A value of 1 means `take into account the entire hemisphere` resulting in blurry occlusion, while a value of 0 means `take into account a single up occlusion direction up` resulting in sharp occlusion.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.OcclusionCombineMode
member.summary: Controls how occlusion from Distance Field Ambient Occlusion is combined with Screen Space Ambient Occlusion.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.RealTimeCapture
member.summary: When enabled, the sky will be captured and convolved to achieve dynamic diffuse and specular environment lighting. SkyAtmosphere, VolumetricCloud Components as well as sky domes with Sky materials are taken into account.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.Cubemap
member.summary: Cubemap to use for sky lighting if SourceType is set to SLS_SpecifiedCubemap.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.SourceCubemapAngle
member.summary: Angle to rotate the source cubemap when SourceType is set to SLS_SpecifiedCubemap.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.OcclusionContrast
member.summary: Contrast S-curve applied to the computed AO. A value of 0 means no contrast increase, 1 is a significant contrast increase.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.OcclusionExponent
member.summary: Exponent applied to the computed AO. Values lower than 1 brighten occlusion overall without losing contact shadows.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.MinOcclusion
member.summary: Controls the darkest that a fully occluded area can get. This tends to destroy contact shadows, use Contrast or OcclusionExponent instead.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.OcclusionTint
member.summary: Tint color on occluded areas, artistic control.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.SetCubemapBlend(UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureCube,UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureCube,System.Single)
member.summary: Creates sky lighting from a blend between two cubemaps, which is only valid when SourceType is set to SpecifiedCubemap. This can be used to seamlessly transition sky lighting between different times of day. The caller should continue to update the blend until BlendFraction is 0 or 1 to reduce rendering cost. The caller is responsible for avoiding pops due to changing the source or destination.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.USkyLightComponent.RecaptureSky
member.summary: Recaptures the scene for the skylight. This is useful for making sure the sky light is up to date after changing something in the world that it would capture. Warning: this is very costly and will definitely cause a hitch.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USoundNodeRandom.RandomizeWithoutReplacement
member.summary:
Determines whether or not this SoundNodeRandom should randomize with or without replacement.
WithoutReplacement means that only nodes left will be valid for selection. So with that, you are guarenteed to have only one occurrence of the sound played until all of the other sounds in the set have all been played.
WithReplacement means that a node will be chosen and then placed back into the set. So one could play the same sound over and over if the probabilities don't go your way :-)

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.USpringArmComponent
member.summary:
This component tries to maintain its children at a fixed distance from the parent, but will retract the children if there is a collision, and spring back when there is no collision.
Example: Use as a 'camera boom' or 'selfie stick' to keep the follow camera for a player from colliding into the world.

member.summary: Natural length of the spring arm when there are no collisions

member.summary: Offset at start of spring, applied in world space. Use this if you want a world-space offset from the parent component instead of the usual relative-space offset.

member.summary: How big should the query probe sphere be (in unreal units)

member.summary: Collision channel of the query probe (defaults to ECC_Camera)

member.summary: If true, do a collision test using ProbeChannel and ProbeSize to prevent camera clipping into level.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.USpringArmComponent.UsePawnControlRotation
member.summary:
If this component is placed on a pawn, should it use the view/control rotation of the pawn where possible? When disabled, the component will revert to using the stored RelativeRotation of the component. Note that this component itself does not rotate, but instead maintains its relative rotation to its parent as normal, and just repositions and rotates its children as desired by the inherited rotation settings. Use GetTargetRotation() if you want the rotation target based on all the settings (UsePawnControlRotation, InheritPitch, etc).
See: GetTargetRotation(), APawn::GetViewRotation()

member.summary: Should we inherit yaw from parent component. Does nothing if using Absolute Rotation.

member.summary: If true and camera location lag is enabled, draws markers at the camera target (in green) and the lagged position (in yellow). A line is drawn between the two locations, in green normally but in red if the distance to the lag target has been clamped (by CameraLagMaxDistance).

member.summary: If bEnableCameraLag is true, controls how quickly camera reaches target position. Low values are slower (more lag), high values are faster (less lag), while zero is instant (no lag).

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh
member.summary:
A StaticMesh is a piece of geometry that consists of a static set of polygons. Static Meshes can be translated, rotated, and scaled, but they cannot have their vertices animated in any way. As such, they are more efficient to render than other types of geometry such as USkeletalMesh, and they are often the basic building block of levels created in the engine.
See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Engine/Content/Types/StaticMeshes/ See: AStaticMeshActor, UStaticMeshComponent

member.summary: The light map resolution

member.summary: The light map coordinate index

member.summary: Whether to support per instance texture color mesh painting on components using this mesh.

member.summary: The default coordinate index to use when texture color painting on this mesh.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.MeshPaintTextureResolution
member.summary: The resolution of texture color mesh paint textures on this mesh. The final size will be rounded up to a power of 2 and a multiple of the "Mesh Paint Tile Size" project setting. A default value of 0 will auto calculate the size using the "Mesh paint texels per vertex" project setting.

member.summary: Useful for reducing self shadowing from distance field methods when using world position offset to animate the mesh's vertices.

member.summary: Specifies which mesh LOD to use for complex (per-poly) collision. Sometimes it can be desirable to use a lower poly representation for collision to reduce memory usage, improve performance and behaviour. Collision representation does not change based on distance to camera.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.GenerateMeshDistanceField
member.summary: Whether to generate a distance field for this mesh, which can be used by DistanceField Indirect Shadows. This is ignored if the project's 'Generate Mesh Distance Fields' setting is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.StripComplexCollisionForConsole_DEPRECATED
member.summary: If true, strips unwanted complex collision data aka kDOP tree when cooking for consoles. On the Playstation 3 data of this mesh will be stored in video memory.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.HasNavigationData
member.summary: If true, mesh will have NavCollision property with additional data for navmesh generation and usage. Set to false for distant meshes (always outside navigation bounds) to save memory on collision data.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.SupportUniformlyDistributedSampling
member.summary: Mesh supports uniformly distributed sampling in constant time. Memory cost is 8 bytes per triangle. Example usage is uniform spawning of particles.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.SupportPhysicalMaterialMasks
member.summary: If true, complex collision data will store UVs and face remap table for use when performing PhysicalMaterialMask lookups in cooked builds. Note the increased memory cost for this functionality.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.SupportRayTracing
member.summary: If true, a ray tracing acceleration structure will be built for this mesh and it may be used in ray tracing effects

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.AllowCPUAccess
member.summary: If true, will keep geometry data CPU-accessible in cooked builds, rather than uploading to GPU memory and releasing it from CPU memory. This is required if you wish to access StaticMesh geometry data on the CPU at runtime in cooked builds (e.g. to convert StaticMesh to ProceduralMeshComponent)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStaticMesh.SupportGpuUniformlyDistributedSampling
member.summary: If true, a GPU buffer containing required data for uniform mesh surface sampling will be created at load time. It is created from the cpu data so bSupportUniformlyDistributedSampling is also required to be true.

member.summary: When using non-blocking streaming requests, upcoming frames are loaded into memory in advance. This property controls how many frames to prefetch.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStreamableSparseVolumeTexture.PrefetchPercentageStepSize
member.summary: When using non-blocking streaming requests, upcoming frames are loaded into memory in advance. This property controls the size reduction in percent of each additional prefetched frames. A value of 20.0 would prefetch frame N+1 at 80%, N+2 at 60%, N+3 at 40% etc.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UStreamableSparseVolumeTexture.PrefetchPercentageBias
member.summary: When using non-blocking streaming requests, upcoming frames are loaded into memory in advance. This property applies a bias in percent to how much data is prefetched for every frame. A value of 20.0 adds 20% to all prefetch percentages. So if PrefetchPercentageStepSize is set to 20.0, frame N+1 is prefetched at 80% + 20% = 100%, frame N+2 at 60% + 20% = 80%, N+3 at 40% + 20% = 60% etc.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingRenderAssetPrimitiveInfo.Bounds
member.summary: The streaming bounds of the texture/mesh, usually the component material bounds. Usually only valid for registered component, as component bounds are only updated when the components are registered. otherwise only PackedRelativeBox can be used.Irrelevant when the component is not registered, as the component could be moved by ULevel::ApplyWorldOffset() In that case, only PackedRelativeBox is meaningful.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingRenderAssetPrimitiveInfo.PackedRelativeBox
member.summary: When non zero, this represents the relative box used to compute Bounds, using the component bounds as reference. If available, this allows the renderable asset streamer to generate the level streaming data before the level gets visible. At that point, the component are not yet registered, and the bounds are unknown, but the precompiled build data is still available. Also allows to update the relative bounds after a level get moved around from ApplyWorldOffset.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingTextureBuildInfo
member.summary: This struct holds the result of TextureStreaming Build for each component texture, as referred by its used materials. It is possible that the entry referred by this data is not actually relevant in a given quality / target. It is also possible that some texture are not referred, and will then fall on fallbacks computation. Because each component holds its precomputed data for each texture, this struct is designed to be as compact as possible.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingTextureBuildInfo.PackedRelativeBox
member.summary: The relative bounding box for this entry. The relative bounds is a bound equal or smaller than the component bounds and represent the merged LOD section bounds of all LOD section referencing the given texture. When the level transform is modified following a call to ApplyLevelTransform, this relative bound becomes deprecated as it was computed from the transform at build time.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingTextureBuildInfo.TextureLevelIndex
member.summary: The level scope identifier of the texture. When building the texture streaming data, each level holds a list of all referred texture Guids. This is required to prevent loading textures on platforms which would not require the texture to be loaded, and is a consequence of the texture streaming build not being platform specific (the same streaming data is build for every platform target). Could also apply to quality level.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FStreamingTextureBuildInfo.TexelFactor
member.summary: The texel factor for this texture. This represent the world size a texture square holding with unit UVs. This value is a combination of the TexelFactor from the mesh and also the material scale. It does not take into consideration StreamingDistanceMultiplier, or texture group scale.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTexture.LevelIndex
member.summary: * Level scope index of this texture. It is used to reduce the amount of lookup to map a texture to its level index. * Useful when building texture streaming data, as well as when filling the texture streamer with precomputed data. * It relates to FStreamingTextureBuildInfo::TextureLevelIndex and also the index in ULevel::StreamingTextureGuids. * Default value of -1, indicates that the texture has an unknown index (not yet processed). At level load time, * -2 is also used to indicate that the texture has been processed but no entry were found in the level table. * After any of these processes, the LevelIndex is reset to INDEX_NONE. Making it ready for the next level task.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings
member.summary: Encoding can either use the "Final" or "Fast" speeds, for supported encoders (e.g. Oodle) Encode speed settings have no effect on encoders that don't support encode speed, currently limited to Oodle.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.SharedLinearTextureEncoding
member.summary:
If true, platforms that want to take a linearly encoded texture and then tile them will try to reuse the linear texture rather than encode it for every platform. This can result in massive speedups for texture building as tiling is very fast compared to encoding. So instead of:
Host Platform: Linear encode Console 1: Linear encode + platform specific tile Console 2: Linear encode + platform specific tile
you instead get: Host platform: Linear encode Console 1: fetch linear + platform specific tile Console 2: fetch linear + platform specific tile
Note that this has no effect on cook time, only build time - once the texture is in the DDC this has no effect.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.FinalUsesRDO
member.summary:
If true, Final encode speed enables rate-distortion optimization on supported encoders to decrease *on disc* size of textures in compressed package files. This rate-distortion tradeoff is controlled via "Lambda". The "LossyCompressionAmount" parameter on textures is used to control it. Specific LossyCompressionAmount values correspond to to RDO lambdas of:
None - Disable RDO for this texture. Lowest - 1 (Least distortion) Low - 10 Medium - 20 High - 30 Highest - 40
If set to Default, then the LossyCompressionAmount in the LODGroup for the texture is used. If that is also Default, then the RDOLambda in these settings is used.
Note that any distortion introduced is on top of, and likely less than, any introduced by the format itself.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.FinalRDOLambda
member.summary:
Ignored if UsesRDO is false. This value is used if a given texture is using "Default" LossyCompressionAmount. Otherwise, the value of LossyCompressionAmount is translated in to a fixed lambda (see UsesRDO tooltip).
Low values (1) represent highest quality (least distortion) results.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.FinalEffortLevel
member.summary: Specifies how much time to take trying for better encoding results.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.FinalUniversalTiling
member.summary: Specifies how to assume textures are laid out on disc. This only applies to Oodle with RDO enabled. 256 KB is a good middle ground. Enabling this will decrease the on-disc sizes of textures for platforms with exposed texture tiling (i.e. consoles), but will slightly increase sizes of textures for platforms with opaque tiling (i.e. desktop).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UTextureEncodingProjectSettings.FastUsesRDO
member.summary:
If true, Final encode speed enables rate-distortion optimization on supported encoders to decrease *on disc* size of textures in compressed package files. This rate-distortion tradeoff is controlled via "Lambda". The "LossyCompressionAmount" parameter on textures is used to control it. Specific LossyCompressionAmount values correspond to to RDO lambdas of:

If set to Default, then the LossyCompressionAmount in the LODGroup for the texture is used. If that is also Default, then the RDOLambda in these settings is used.
Note that any distortion introduced is on top of, and likely less than, any introduced by the format itself.

member.summary: Format of the texture render target. Data written to the render target will be quantized to this format, which can limit the range and precision. member.summary: Provides local control over volumetric lightmap density. Only convex shapes supported.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.AVolumetricLightmapDensityVolume.AllowedMipLevelRange
member.summary:
The Volumetric Lightmap has 3 mipmaps, where the highest density mipmap (mip0) corresponds to VolumetricLightmapDetailCellSize. mip0: DetailCellSize mip1: DetailCellSize * 4 mip2: DetailCellSize * 16
By default, highest density will be placed around static geometry and static lights, but AllowedMipLevelRange can be used to override this behavior. Examples: [0, 3] = Volume does nothing [1, 3] = Volume removes highest density mip, even near static geometry, which can be useful to save memory ('stat MapBuildData') [0, 0] = Volume forces highest density. Warning: using this on a large area can greatly increase memory and build times! When multiple volumes overlap, the smallest (highest density) values will be used.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.FWorldContext
member.summary:
FWorldContext A context for dealing with UWorlds at the engine level. As the engine brings up and destroys world, we need a way to keep straight what world belongs to what.
WorldContexts can be thought of as a track. By default we have 1 track that we load and unload levels on. Adding a second context is adding a second track; another track of progression for worlds to live on.
For the GameEngine, there will be one WorldContext until we decide to support multiple simultaneous worlds. For the EditorEngine, there may be one WorldContext for the EditorWorld and one for the PIE World.
FWorldContext provides both a way to manage 'the current PIE UWorld*' as well as state that goes along with connecting/travelling to new worlds.
FWorldContext should remain internal to the UEngine classes. Outside code should not keep pointers or try to manage FWorldContexts directly. Outside code can still deal with UWorld*, and pass UWorld*s into Engine level functions. The Engine code can look up the relevant context for a given UWorld*.
For convenience, FWorldContext can maintain outside pointers to UWorld*s. For example, PIE can tie UWorld* UEditorEngine::PlayWorld to the PIE world context. If the PIE UWorld changes, the UEditorEngine::PlayWorld pointer will be automatically updated. This is done with AddRef() and SetCurrentWorld().

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.AWorldSettings.MinimizeBSPSections
member.summary: Causes the BSP build to generate as few sections as possible. This is useful when you need to reduce draw calls but can reduce texture streaming efficiency and effective lightmap resolution. Note - changes require a rebuild to propagate. Note that any lighting and shadowing interactions that are usually precomputed will be lost if this is enabled.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.UEnhancedInputComponent
member.summary:
Implement an Actor component for input bindings.
An Enhanced Input Component is a transient component that enables an Actor to bind enhanced actions to delegate functions, or monitor those actions. Input components are processed from a stack managed by the PlayerController and processed by the PlayerInput. These bindings will not consume input events, but this behaviour can be replicated using UInputMappingContext::Priority.
See: https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/Input/index.html

member.summary: The prioirty that should be given to this mapping context when it is added

member.summary: If true, then this IMC will be applied immediately when the EI subsystem is ready

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EDeadZoneType.Axial
member.summary: Apply dead zone to axes individually. This will result in input being chamfered at the corners for 2d/3d axis inputs, and matches the original UE4 deadzone logic.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EDeadZoneType.Radial
member.summary:
Apply dead zone logic to all axes simultaneously. This gives smooth input (circular/spherical coverage). On a 1d axis input this works identically to Axial.
For most games, this will give the smoothest feeling analog values. The input is smoothed to avoid "jumpiness" when you are moving the analog axis.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EDeadZoneType.UnscaledRadial
member.summary:
Apply dead zone logic to all axes simultaneously without any smooth input which the normal "Radial" deadzone applies.
The behavior of this deadzone type is as follows: If the magnitude of the input is less then the lower threshold, ignore it. Clamp the magnitude of the input to the upper threshold value.
For some games, this may result in feeling "jumpy", because the value goes from 0.0 to the lower threshold immediately instead of being smoothed, like the normal "Radial" deadzone option.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EFOVScalingType.Standard
member.summary: FOV scaling to apply scaled movement deltas to inputs dependent upon the player's selected FOV

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EFOVScalingType.UE4_BackCompat
member.summary: FOV scaling was incorrectly calculated in UE4's UPlayerInput::MassageAxisInput. This implementation is intended to aid backwards compatibility, but should not be used by new projects.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EInputActionAccumulationBehavior
member.summary: This is an advanced setting that allows you to change how the value of an Input Action is calculated when there are multiple mappings to the same Input Action. The default behavior is to accept highest absolute value.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EInputActionAccumulationBehavior.TakeHighestAbsoluteValue
member.summary:
Take the value from the mapping with the highest Absolute Value.
For example, given a value of -0.3 and 0.5, the input action's value would be 0.5.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.EInputActionAccumulationBehavior.Cumulative
member.summary:
Cumulatively adds the key values for each mapping.
For example, a value of -0.7 and +0.75 on the same input action would result in a value of 0.05.
A practical example of when to use this would be for something like WASD movement, if you want pressing W and S to cancel each other out.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.UEnhancedInputUserSettings
member.summary:
The Enhanced Input User Settings class is a place where you can put all of your Input Related settings that you want your user to be able to change. Things like their key mappings, aim sensitivity, accessibility settings, etc. This also provides a Registration point for Input Mappings Contexts (IMC) from possibly unloaded plugins (i.e. Game Feature Plugins). You can register your IMC from a Game Feature Action plugin here, and then have access to all the key mappings available. This is very useful for building settings screens because you can now access all the mappings in your game, even if the entire plugin isn't loaded yet.
The user settings are stored on each UEnhancedPlayerInput object, so each instance of the settings can represent a single User or Local Player.
To customize this for your game, you can create a subclass of it and change the "UserSettingsClass" in the Enhanced Input Project Settings.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.UEnhancedInputWorldSubsystem
member.summary:
Per world input subsystem that allows you to bind input delegates to actors without an owning Player Controller. This should be used when an actor needs to receive input delegates but will never have an owning Player Controller. For example, you can add input delegates to unlock a door when the user has a certain set of keys pressed. Be sure to enable input on the actor, or else the input delegates won't fire!
Note: if you do have an actor with an owning Player Controller use the local player input subsystem instead.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.UInputAction
member.summary:
An Input Action is a logical representation of something the user can do, such as "Jump" or "Crouch". These are what your gameplay code binds to in order to listen for input state changes. For most scenarios your gameplay code should be listening for the "Triggered" event on an input action. This will allow for the most scalable and customizable input configuration because you can add different triggers for each key mapping in the Input Mapping Context.
They are the conceptual equivalent to "Action" and "Axis" mapping names from the Legacy Input System.
Note: These are instanced per player (via FInputActionInstance)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.EnhancedInput.UInputAction.AccumulationBehavior
member.summary:
This defines how the value of this input action will be calcuated in the case that there are multiple key mappings to the same input action.
When TakeHighestAbsoluteValue is selected, then the key mapping with the highest absolutle value will be utilized. (Default) When Cumulative is selected, then each key mapping will be added together to get the key value.
See: UEnhancedPlayerInput::ProcessActionMappingEvent, where this property is read from.
